subject: Control plane commit escalation and QoS thresholds
messages:
From: Alya Martin <alya@streamfound.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commit increase & QoS questions

Hi Vivek / Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We finished an internal forecast and expect a sustained increase in inference volume over the next 12 months — projection attached (streamfound_usage_forecast.xlsx). At a high level: average tokens/month would move from ~150M to ~650M, with short spikes that could be 3–4x our baseline for up to 45 minutes during product launches.

Before we get to procurement, two quick asks: 1) can Redwood support a stepped commit increase (monthly) to get to that volume without materially higher per-token rate, and 2) what throttling/guardrails do you implement for burst traffic so our UX doesn’t degrade during launches? Streams of short-lived spikes are the main risk for us.

We’re targeting contract signatures the week of Apr 10. I can loop in procurement (cc’d ProcureOps) if that helps.

—Alya
Alya Martin
Head of Product, StreamFound
alya@streamfound.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alya Martin <alya@streamfound.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit increase & QoS questions

Thanks, Alya — and thanks for the forecast. I reviewed the sheet and copied a short proposal (attached: proposed_commit_schedule.xlsx) that outlines a three-step monthly commit ramp with an initial trial uplift, mid-year committed increase, and an end-of-year floor.

A few operational notes up front:
- We can support a stepped commit path to 650M tokens/month with no step-change to per-token pricing if you accept staged minimums (details in the attachment).
- For burst protection we recommend a QoS policy: prefix caching + soft-rate ceiling per route and a short-term burst buffer (we call it the "launch buffer"). Typical config we recommend: 30 RPS per model-route soft cap with a 5–10 minute burst allowance (up to 3x) backed by auto-fallback to a lower-capacity variant when capacity is constrained.
- We can also enable a canary policy for each launch window (route-level mirroring + 5% traffic to new rollout) if you want extra safety.

I’ll pull in Rishi and Lauren to align on commercials and the DocuSign path. If you’re free tomorrow I can do a 30-minute sync to walk the schedule and the QoS playbook.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Alya Martin <alya@streamfound.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit increase & QoS questions

Alya — quick commercial note from our side. We can structure pricing as follows (summary):
1) Q2 trial uplift: 200M committed (monthly) for 3 months at current hosted price, with a $0.0009 per-token cranking for overage beyond buffer.
2) Q3–Q4 ramp: move to 450M committed/month with a step discount applied to the hosted tier; per-token pricing steps down as commits increase (see redwood_quote_v3.pdf).
3) Annual floor: 650M committed/month with a corporate discount and a burst credit pool.

Operational guardrails (to align with Vivek’s notes):
- Soft per-route RPS cap: 30 RPS (internal routing) with an elastic burst window up to 90 RPS for 5–10 minutes.
- If sustained 15-minute average exceeds 2x baseline, auto-fallback to a cheaper, higher-latency variant is triggered and ops is notified.
- We can bake in an SLA credit schedule if performance falls below agreed latency percentiles during agreed launch windows.

Lauren — can you prepare a draft amendment with these tiers + a short exhibit describing the burst credit accounting?

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Alya Martin <alya@streamfound.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procureops@streamfound.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit increase & QoS questions

Thanks — that structure looks reasonable. A couple follow-ups from procurement:
- They want the canary + fallback behavior and the SLA credit mechanics in writing (ProcureOps attached a procurement intake PDF).
- They asked for a short operational runbook that our SREs can validate ahead of the first launch window (can you provide a sample?).
- On billing: we prefer monthly invoicing with a single line item for committed tokens + a separate line for overages.

ProcureOps will be driving contract language and will expect our procurement system to receive a signed amendment by Apr 12 to meet internal timelines. Are you able to make that date?

—Alya

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alya Martin <alya@streamfound.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit increase & QoS questions

Alya — looping in the commercial artifact. I’ve drafted an amendment (attached: redwood_quote_v3.pdf) that mirrors the stepped-commit path Rishi outlined and a short exhibit for burst credit accounting. I also uploaded a one-page runbook (qos_thresholds.pdf) that outlines the canary flow, fallback rules, and operational contacts.

DocuSign link below for the amendment; it contains placeholders for the launch windows and SLA tiers which we can finalize post-signature if you prefer the commercial cadence locked first.
- DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/embedded/sign?docId=9f3e

If ProcureOps needs any contract language tweaks, happy to triage — we can usually turn simple redlines in 24–48 hours.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Sales Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alya Martin <alya@streamfound.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit increase & QoS questions

Alya — appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps from Redwood:
1) We will issue the amendment and DocuSign by EOD today with the stepped-commit tiers you approved (trial uplift -> mid-year -> annual floor).
2) Lauren will include the burst-credit exhibit and the monthly invoicing format.
3) We will share the operational runbook (qos_thresholds.pdf) with your SREs and schedule a 45-minute technical sync in the first week after signature to validate canary/fallback behavior.
4) Exhaustive SLA and credit mechanics will be attached as an exhibit; operationally the fallback path will be automatic but observable via our Console (route-level dashboards and alerts).

Hannah — I’m looping you in for approval on the SLA exhibit and any legal escalation if ProcureOps raises non-standard terms.

Alya — if you can confirm the DocuSign signers and ProcureOps point-of-contact I’ll make sure procurement receives the final packet today.

Thanks all — let’s get this over the finish line.

Regards,
Vivek
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
